# fastf 3.19.0: your shell in the project folder, right where the app is

`X` starts the agent in the project's folder in the app's own terminal. `$`
now does the same for your shell. Press it on a project and the app steps
aside, your shell (`$SHELL`) starts in that project's folder, and `exit`
brings the app back where you left it.

- **No setup.** Nothing goes into your `.bashrc`. fastf starts a shell in
  the folder, the way it starts the agent; it never moves the shell you
  started fastf from.
- **Works over ssh.** `t` opens a new terminal window and needs a desktop
  for it; `$` uses the terminal you are already in.
- **Your shell as you know it.** It starts the way a terminal tab starts it,
  with your prompt, aliases and `PATH`. On Windows it is PowerShell.

`t` is now titled "Open a terminal window", so the pair reads like `x` and
`X`: a window of its own, or here.

## Ctrl-C belongs to what you are running

Ctrl-C typed to an agent `X` started could reach fastf too. Once the agent
was done, the app quit with `aborted.`, and a second Ctrl-C closed fastf
while the agent was still running. Now Ctrl-C goes only to the agent, or to
the command running in the `$` shell. Closing the window still closes fastf.

`fastf term` on the command line still opens a new window. A command cannot
move the shell it was typed into; `cd "$(fastf path ID0047)"` does that.

How it works: [docs/app.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/app.md)
